about: Review of branch manual-only before 1.5 (workflow wf_de22bae8-d34, 2026-09-26): 4 reviewers (engine, views, remote, spec), 2 skeptics per finding. upheld = skeptics who could not refute it. Fixed: the tooltip early-switch number, protocol 1 in docs and the integration script. The rest were deferred as minor (see docs/SESSION-HANDOVER.md).

confirmed.title: removeAccount's new fallback only changes PixelSwitch's label: the switchTo it starts does nothing, so the fallback account gets the removed account's live usage (pre-existing, but it defeats the new Manual only fallback)
confirmed.scenario: The founder removes the active account X, whose login Claude Code is using. removeAccount marks the fallback F (the first account that is not Manual only) as active and sets activeAccount = F, then starts Task { await switchTo(F) }. In performSwitch, currentActive is already F. provenOwner(live credential) returns nil because X is no longer in `accounts`, so the condition `liveOwner == nil && currentActive.id == account.id` is true and it logs 'No switch needed' and returns. Claude Code keeps running on X's login while PixelSwitch shows F as Active. fetchAllAccountUsage reads the active account's usage from keychain.readClaudeToken(), so F is credited with X's usage. Auto-switch then decides from those wrong readings, for example moving off F because X was at 95%. reconcileLiveLogin never repairs this, because the live login has no known owner. The old code had the same flaw with `accounts.first`. The new log line 'switching to <fallback id>' and the careful choice of a non Manual only fallback have no effect on the real login.
confirmed.evidence: AppState.swift:720-725: `accounts[index].isActive = true; activeAccount = accounts[index]; ... Task { await switchTo(fallback) }`. AppState.swift:777: `if liveOwner?.id == account.id || (liveOwner == nil && currentActive.id == account.id) { log.info("[switchTo] No switch needed..."); return }`. AppState.swift:1411-1412 reads the active account's usage from the live token.
confirmed.fix: Keep activeAccount pointing at the removed account (or at nil with a force path) until the switch finishes, so performSwitch sees a real 'from' account and writes F's credential. Alternatively, add a parameter to performSwitch that skips the 'already live' shortcut when the live credential's owner is unknown. Mark F active only after the switch completes.
verdicts:
UPHELD (minor): I traced the scenario through the code and it happens as described. The trash button in AccountSwitcherView.swift:218 is shown on the active row too, so an active account can be removed. So can a call through AppController.removeAccount:152.

What happens, step by step:
1. removeAccount (AppState.swift:709-729) deletes X's backup (keychain.removeAccountBackup) and removes X from `accounts`.
2. It then marks the fallback F active, sets activeAccount = F, and schedules Task { await switchTo(F) }.
3. In performSwitch (748-781), currentActive is already F.
4. The live credential is still X's. provenOwner -> account(matching:) finds no owner: X is gone from `accounts`, so the email match finds nothing, and X's backup was just deleted, so the accountUuid match finds nothing. liveOwner is nil.
5. Line 777, `liveOwner == nil && currentActive.id == account.id`, is therefore true. It logs "No switch needed" and returns, so F's credential is never written.
6. reconcileLiveLogin (959-961) returns at once when provenOwner is nil, so it never repairs this.
7. fetchAllAccountUsage (1410-1411) reads the active account's usage from keychain.readClaudeToken(). F is therefore credited with X's live usage, and auto-switch decides from those readings.

The old code (`accounts.first`, same shortcut) had the same flaw, so this change did not introduce it. The new code matches the spec's removeAccount block exactly. But the spec's intent ("switching to <fallback>", the careful Manual only fallback choice) does not happen for the real login. It is a real defect the founder would hit, so it cannot be refuted. I rate it minor: it predates this change, and this change only makes it more visible.

UPHELD (minor): I could not refute it. The chain holds against the code, but the bug is older than this branch and the change does not make it worse. Traced: removeAccount (AppState.swift:711-725) deletes X's keychain backup and removes X from `accounts`. It then marks F active and sets activeAccount = F before `Task { await switchTo(fallback) }` runs. In performSwitch, provenOwner(liveCredential) (line 878) goes through account(matching:) (line 858). That function matches only by the accountUuid in a backup (X's was just deleted) or by an email in `accounts` (X is gone), so it returns nil even when the API answers. The shortcut at line 777, `liveOwner == nil && currentActive.id == account.id`, is then true, and the switch logs 'No switch needed' and returns. Claude Code keeps running on X's login. reconcileLiveLogin (line 961) returns early on the same nil owner, so it never repairs this. fetchAllAccountUsage (line 1411-1412) and fetchUsageNow (line 1176) read the active account's usage from keychain.readClaudeToken(), so F shows X's numbers, and auto-switch decides from them. There is no data loss: ClaudeService.switchAccount skips the step-1 backup when the owner is unproven, so F's saved login is never overwritten with X's. How it looks to the founder: he removes the account he is signed in to (trash button in the popover, or `pixelswitch accounts remove`). PixelSwitch then shows F as Active with X's session and weekly figures, while Claude Code still bills X. It stays that way until some later switch, manual or automatic, writes a real credential. Why this is minor: main had the same code with `accounts.first` in place of the fallback. The spec (final-spec.json, engineChanges) says outright 'Unchanged: switchTo, performSwitch', so the branch matches its spec. It only takes removing the account that is live right now. It fixes itself on the next switch and loses nothing. It is worth a follow-up, for example marking F active only after the switch completes, or skipping the 'already live' shortcut when the live login's owner is unknown. It is not a regression from the Manual only work.

confirmed.title: Row tooltip says an account is switched to 'only while it is at 80% or less', but under Resets soonest the early drain moves you to it at up to 89%
confirmed.scenario: The founder sets 'Choose the next account by' to Resets soonest. 'Switch early to use quota before it resets' is on by default. An account on the default of 90% shows the tooltip 'Auto-switch moves you off this account at 90%, and moves you to it only while it is at 80% or less.' But drainEligibleUtilization uses ceiling(T, room: drainMinimumRoom) = 89, so the early drain moves him to that account at 85%. The tooltip claims to use 'the same function the engine ranks and verifies with', yet it only describes the threshold rule. The same gap appears for low thresholds: a 10% account is drained to at up to 9%, while the tooltip says 5%.
confirmed.evidence: SettingsAccountsTab.swift:199 `let arriveAt = AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling(threshold: leaveAt, room: AutoSwitchEngine.hysteresis) ?? 0`, compared with AutoSwitchEngine.swift:168 `Self.ceiling(threshold: threshold, room: drainMinimumRoom)` for the drain rule.
confirmed.fix: When AutoSwitchSettings.strategy == .resetsSoonest and drainEarly is on, add a clause giving the drain ceiling, e.g. '(or at N% or less when its weekly quota is about to reset)'. Or word the tooltip so it applies only to the threshold rule.
verdicts:
UPHELD (minor): I could not refute it. The scenario is real, and the tooltip makes a claim the engine does not keep.

1. The tooltip (SettingsAccountsTab.swift:199-200) works out its second number as `ceiling(threshold: leaveAt, room: hysteresis)`, which is 80 for a 90% account. It then says the account is switched to "only while it is at 80% or less".

2. The early-drain rule does not use that number. `plan()` runs the drain branch (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:298) when four things hold: the active account has not reached its threshold, the active account is not Manual only, the strategy is `.resetsSoonest`, and `drainEarly` is on. `drainEarly` is on by default (`?? true`). `drainEligibleUtilization` (line 168) caps the target at `ceiling(threshold:, room: drainMinimumRoom)`, which is 89 at 90% and 4 at 5%. A 10% account gets 9, not the 5 the tooltip shows.

3. So with Resets soonest selected, an account at 85% whose weekly reset is within 24 hours and earlier than the active account's can be drained to, even though its tooltip says 80% or less. That strategy is not the default, but the founder can pick it in Settings. The spec's own risk note calls the tooltip's "at 2.5% or less" for a 5% account "exact", yet the drain would take that account at up to 4%.

The code does copy the spec's tooltip text and formula exactly. But the spec gives its reason as "so the words cannot drift from the rule", and here the numbers do drift from the drain rule, so this is a gap in the spec rather than something it meant. The spec's "deliberately not reworded" note is about the early-switch help text in General settings, not this tooltip. The old tooltip made no claim about when an account is switched to, so this branch adds the wrong claim.

This is a copy problem only. Switching itself is correct, and it only shows up with Resets soonest selected, so it stays minor.

UPHELD (minor): I could not refute this. The finding is real, but it only shows up under a setting that is not the default.

What the code does: `SettingsAccountsTab.swift:198-200` builds the row tooltip from `ceiling(threshold: leaveAt, room: AutoSwitchEngine.hysteresis)`. For an account on the default 90%, that reads "moves you to it only while it is at 80% or less." The early-drain path works differently. It is `AutoSwitchEngine.drainEligibleUtilization` (line 168), which uses `ceiling(threshold:room: drainMinimumRoom)`, so 89 for T=90 and 9 for T=10. `AppState` checks the target with the same `.drainEarly` rule, so the switch really goes through. Early drain runs only when all of these hold:
- the strategy is "Resets soonest" (the default is Most room left, per `AutoSwitchSettings.strategy`)
- "Switch early to use quota before it resets" is on (it defaults to true)
- the target's weekly reset is within the drain window (24 hours by default) and sooner than the active account's
- the active account is not Manual only and has not reached its threshold

In that case the founder can be moved to an account at 81-89%, even though its tooltip just said "only while it is at 80% or less". That is exactly the case the drain was built for: his own example of an account with about 5% left before it resets. He asked for Resets soonest and early switching, so this setup is plausible.

The code matches the spec: `final-spec.json` asks for this exact sentence and the hysteresis ceiling. So the fault is in the spec, not the implementation. The spec's claim that "the words cannot drift from the rule" overlooked the drain rule.

The same gap is in the new MCP `set_account_threshold` description in `PixelSwitchCLI/MCPServer.swift`: "another account is switched to only while it is at least 10 points under its own threshold." That is also false under early drain. The Settings -> General paragraph is fine, because it describes only the threshold case, and the drain toggle has its own help text ("...and that account still has room").

Severity: minor. Switching is correct, no data is lost, and nothing crashes. The wrong text is a hover tooltip and an MCP description, it is only wrong in the Resets soonest plus early-drain mode, and the drain's own help text in Settings describes that exception. Fix: add a drain clause when the strategy is Resets soonest and early drain is on, or reword the tooltip and the MCP text so they cover only the threshold rule.

confirmed.title: Row tooltip says 'moves you to it only while it is at X% or less', which is false when early switching is on
confirmed.scenario: Set Settings → General → 'Choose the next account by' to Resets soonest and keep 'Switch early to use quota before it resets' on (it is on by default for that strategy). Take the founder's default of 98 and hover an account on Default. The tooltip says 'Auto-switch moves you off this account at 98%, and moves you to it only while it is at 88% or less.' The early switch still moves you to that account at up to 97%, because drainEligibleUtilization uses ceiling(threshold, drainMinimumRoom = 1). For a 10% account the tooltip says 5% while the early switch accepts up to 9%. The 'moves you off at 98%' half is also wrong in this mode, since the early switch can move you off sooner. The founder currently uses mostRoom, so he would only see this after changing strategy. The text matches the spec word for word, but the spec only checked it against the threshold rule.
confirmed.fix: Either drop 'only', or read the strategy and early-switch settings with @AppStorage and, when both are on, add a second number from AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling(threshold: leaveAt, room: AutoSwitchEngine.drainMinimumRoom). For example: '…at 88% or less (97% or less for an early switch)'. A new key would need adding to all five tables.
verdicts: UPHELD (minor): I traced the code and the finding holds. SettingsAccountsTab.thresholdHelp works out the second number only from AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling(threshold: leaveAt, room: AutoSwitchEngine.hysteresis), which is 10 points under the threshold, or half the threshold below 20. It then says auto-switch moves you to the account "only" at or under that number. The early switch works differently. AutoSwitchEngine.drainEligibleUtilization (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:168) uses ceiling(threshold:room: drainMinimumRoom = 1), which is 1 point under the threshold. rankedTargets and AppState's check both reach it through eligibleUtilization(trigger: .drainEarly). plan() runs that path whenever no threshold was reached, the active account is not Manual only, the strategy is .resetsSoonest and the early switch is on. AutoSwitchSettings.drainEarly defaults to true (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:461, and the SettingsView @AppStorage default is also true). So with Resets soonest picked, a Default account on a 98% default whose weekly reset is sooner can be switched to at up to 97%, while the tooltip says 88%. A 10% account can be switched to at up to 9%, while the tooltip says 5%. The spec's own test expects exactly that ("a 10% account at 9% has room"). The tooltip matches the spec word for word, but the spec says the number is there "so the words cannot drift from the rule", and it only checked the threshold rule. The line about the early-switch help being "deliberately not reworded" refers to a different string. So this is a gap in the spec, not wording it chose on purpose. It is only minor because the founder uses Most room left, which is the default, and nothing about switching behaviour is wrong. It is just an inaccurate tooltip in one non-default mode.

UPHELD (minor): The finding is real, but the founder does not see it today, and when he does it is a small wording error. I checked the code on the branch (PixelSwitch/Views/SettingsAccountsTab.swift, thresholdHelp). The tooltip works out its "arrive at" number as AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling(threshold: leaveAt, room: hysteresis), which is 10 points under the threshold. The early switch uses a different number. drainEligibleUtilization (PixelSwitch/Services/AutoSwitchEngine.swift, line 168) uses ceiling(threshold, room: drainMinimumRoom = 1). plan() runs that path when strategy == .resetsSoonest and drainEarly is on, which is the default because AutoSwitchSettings.drainEarly reads unset as true. So under Resets soonest, a Default-98 account can be switched to at up to 97%, yet its tooltip says "only while it is at 88% or less". A 10% account shows "5%" but accepts up to 9%. The word "only" is literally false there. The change added it: the old tooltip ("When this account's usage reaches this level, auto-switch moves you to another account") made no such claim.

Who actually sees it: I read the founder's live defaults. autoSwitchStrategy = mostRoom, autoSwitchEnabled = 1, autoSwitchThreshold = 98, and autoSwitchDrainEarly is unset (reads as on). With mostRoom the early switch never runs, so today every tooltip number is correct. He would only see the wrong number after changing the strategy to Resets soonest. Even then, three things keep it small:
- The early switch only picks an account whose weekly reset is within the drain window (24h by default) and sooner than the active account's.
- The text is a hover tooltip.
- The General tab's early-switch help text already says it "Switches before the active account reaches its threshold when another account's weekly quota resets within this many hours...".

The "moves you off at X%" half is not false, because the threshold still moves him off there. It just leaves out that he can be moved off sooner. The Manual only tooltip is accurate, because plan() never early-drains an active Manual only account. The code matches the spec word for word, so this is a hole in the spec, not code that departs from it. Nothing about switching behaviour is wrong. It is a misleading number in one tooltip, under a strategy the founder does not use, so the severity is minor.

confirmed.title: Integration check still expects remote-control protocol 1, so it fails against this build
confirmed.scenario: The founder installs the build with this change and runs Tests/integration/remote-control.sh, as the worklog's follow-ups tell every release to do. `pixelswitch --json status` now returns protocolVersion 2, so check 1 prints 'FAIL  status protocol', the script ends with '1 failed' and exits non-zero. The 572 unit tests do not run this script, so nothing caught it. The header comment (line 14, 'Needs PixelSwitch 1.2 or later') is also wrong now: a pixelswitch built from this branch refuses every app older than this release.
confirmed.evidence: Line 47: `[ "$(echo "$status" | field protocolVersion)" = "1" ] && ok "status answers, protocol 1" || bad "status protocol" "$status"`. ControlProtocol.swift:13 is now `static let version = 2`.
confirmed.fix: Compare against 2 (or parse the number from `"$CLI" --version`, which prints 'remote-control protocol N', so the next bump cannot break the script again). Change the PASS text to match, and change line 14 to 'Needs PixelSwitch 1.5 or later'.
verdicts:
UPHELD (minor): The finding is real. The branch does not touch Tests/integration/remote-control.sh; it is not in `git diff main...manual-only --stat`. Line 47 still reads `[ "$(echo "$status" | field protocolVersion)" = "1" ] && ok "status answers, protocol 1" || bad "status protocol" "$status"`.

The code path, end to end:
- `pixelswitch --json status` goes to CLIRunner `case .status`. It calls `.statusGet` and prints the raw result (`show(result)` prints `result.prettyText` when json is on).
- In the app, ControlAPI.swift:228 fills in `protocolVersion: ControlProtocol.version`.
- ControlProtocol.swift:13 is now `static let version = 2`.

So against any build from this branch, check 1 prints "FAIL  status protocol", `fail` goes up and the script ends non-zero.

The spec asks for the bump ("ControlProtocol.swift: version 2") and says nothing about the integration script, so this is stale test code left behind by the bump, not intended behaviour. The unit tests cannot catch it because they do not run this script. The header line "Needs PixelSwitch 1.2 or later" is also stale: CLIRunner.checkProtocol makes a CLI from this branch refuse any app older than this release.

Severity is minor, not important. The app, CLI and MCP all behave correctly. Only the manual check fails, it runs against the real app when the worklog follow-ups say to, and the FAIL line prints the status JSON showing protocolVersion 2, so the cause is obvious. The fix is one line: compare against 2, or read the number from `pixelswitch --version`, and update the PASS text and the header.

UPHELD (minor): The defect is real, but it is smaller than reported. The branch sets ControlProtocol.version to 2 (PixelSwitch/Control/ControlProtocol.swift:13). ControlAPI.swift:228 returns that number as status.protocolVersion. The diff does not touch Tests/integration/remote-control.sh, and its line 47 still checks `= "1"`. So against a build from this branch, check 1 prints 'FAIL  status protocol', the summary shows 1 failed, and the script exits non-zero. The worklog (docs/worklog/2026-09-25.md lines 248, 282, 322) and the Part C plan tell the next session to run this script after each install, and the plan expects every line to be PASS. The next session will therefore see a false failure and may chase it. The spec calls for the bump to version 2 on purpose, and nothing in the spec updates the script, so nobody caught it.

The founder never sees this in the app, the CLI or MCP. The app and the pixelswitch tool come from the same build (the tool ships in Contents/Helpers), so they agree on version 2 and every real command works. The only visible effect is one wrong FAIL line in a developer check script, and the other checks still run.

The claim about the header comment (line 14, 'Needs PixelSwitch 1.2 or later') is only partly right. CLIRunner.checkProtocol already refuses a mismatched app with 'Quit and reopen PixelSwitch', so an old app gives a clear message rather than a silent failure. The header is stale documentation, not a behaviour bug.

The fix is small: compare against 2, or read the number from `pixelswitch --version`. That makes this a test-tooling defect, so minor rather than important.

confirmed.title: ARCHITECTURE.md still says remote-control protocol version 1
confirmed.scenario: A later session reads the Remote control section to learn the protocol, sees 'protocol version 1', and either doubts the code or 'fixes' a test back to 1. The task asked for docs that state protocol 1 to be updated, and this line was missed.
confirmed.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:575: "(`PixelSwitch/Control/ControlProtocol.swift`, compiled into the app and the tool, protocol version 1)". The branch bumps ControlProtocol.version to 2 and adds AccountInfo.manualOnly.
confirmed.fix: Change it to 'protocol version 2 (1.5: AccountInfo.manualOnly; accounts.setThreshold takes 0–100)', or drop the literal number and point to ControlProtocol.version.
verdicts:
UPHELD (minor): I could not refute this. The stale line is real. On manual-only, ARCHITECTURE.md:575 still says "(`PixelSwitch/Control/ControlProtocol.swift`, compiled into the app and the tool, protocol version 1)". ARCHITECTURE.md is not in `git diff main...manual-only --stat`. ControlProtocol.swift on the branch has `static let version = 2`, up from 1 on main, and AccountInfo gains the required `manualOnly` field. So the project's own architecture doc, the one CLAUDE.md points readers to, now gives the wrong protocol number.

Two parts of the finding go too far. First, final-spec.json never mentions ARCHITECTURE.md; its doc list covers only README lines 73, 131 and 134. So "the task asked for docs that state protocol 1 to be updated" is not backed by the spec. Second, the harm scenario is weak. ControlTests.swift:86 checks `ControlProtocol.version == 2`, so if someone "fixed" the test back to 1, it would fail against the code instead of quietly passing.

Nobody using the app, CLI or MCP sees this, and switching behaviour is unaffected. It is documentation drift, so minor.

UPHELD (minor): The stale line is real. ARCHITECTURE.md:575 still says "protocol version 1". ARCHITECTURE.md is not in the diff (git diff main...manual-only --stat lists 22 files, none of them ARCHITECTURE.md). ControlProtocol.version was 1 on main and is 2 on the branch.

The founder would not see it in the running app, the CLI or MCP. Every place that shows a version reads ControlProtocol.version from the code. That covers `pixelswitch --version` (CLIRunner.swift:38), the status line (CLIRunner.swift:252), the version-mismatch guard (CLIRunner.swift:64-66) and ControlAPI.swift:228. So nothing a user sees shows the wrong number.

Part of the reviewer's claim is wrong. They say the task asked for docs that state protocol 1 to be updated, but final-spec.json never mentions ARCHITECTURE.md. Its only docs item is three README.md line edits, and the author did change README.md. So the missed line is not a gap against the spec either.

What remains is documentation drift. ARCHITECTURE.md is listed in CLAUDE.md as the reference doc, so a later session could be misled by it. That is minor polish, a one-word fix at ARCHITECTURE.md:575, with no effect on behaviour.

split.title: Races during an await can move you off an active Manual only account below the default, or land a switch on an account that was just set to Manual only
split.scenario: Say the active account A has its own threshold of 70 and sits at 75%. The plan fires and auto-switch starts a fresh verification fetch for candidate B, which takes about a second. During that second the founder sets A to Manual only in Settings, so A should now be left only at the default of 90. When the fetch returns, the re-check guard looks only at isLoggingIn, isRefreshing, isSwitching and the active id. It never looks at A's rule again, so he is moved off A at 75%. The spec says 'Setting Manual only on the account you are using never, on its own, moves you off it.' The target side has the same kind of gap: after verification passes, performSwitch awaits provenOwner and validatedTargetBackup (network calls, sometimes a token refresh) before it writes credentials. An account set to Manual only during those awaits is still switched to, which contradicts the spec's 'cannot be landed on'. Both windows are narrow, about one network round trip.
split.evidence: AppState.swift:1141 `guard !isLoggingIn, !isRefreshing, !isSwitching, activeAccount?.id == active.id else { ... return }` runs after `await fetchUsageNow(for: target)` (line 1110). The active account's rule was read only inside plan() (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:272-277) and is never read again. performSwitch (lines 771-796) awaits provenOwner and validatedTargetBackup with no threshold check before the credential write.
split.fix: In the re-check at line 1141, read the active account's rule again. For trigger .threshold, recompute leaveAtThreshold(rule: effectiveSwitchThreshold(for: active), defaultThreshold:) and stand down unless utilization(accountUsage[active.id], limit:) is still at or above it. For .drainEarly, stand down if the active account is now Manual only. For the target side, pass an 'automatic' flag into performSwitch, or re-check eligibleUtilization for the target right before claudeService.switchAccount when the switch was automatic.
verdicts: REFUTED (minor): Both timing windows exist, but the spec knowingly accepts them and this branch did not create them. (1) Target side: the spec's "AppState checks the chosen target ... using a threshold read fresh by id after the await ... cannot be landed on. No extra check or re-check code is needed" and "Unchanged: switchTo, performSwitch" show the author meant only the verification-fetch window to be covered. The code does cover it. effectiveSwitchThreshold (AppState.swift:657) reads the account from `accounts` by id, and it runs after `await fetchUsageNow`. So an account set to Manual only while it is being checked gets ceiling(0) = nil, logs "manual only now; trying next" and is skipped. The only gap left is the provenOwner/validatedTargetBackup awaits inside performSwitch, which the spec deliberately leaves untouched. On main, any threshold edit can race that same window. (2) Active side: the re-check guard at line 1141 is word for word the same as on main (line 1134 there). On main, raising A's own threshold from 70 to 90 during the verification fetch moves him off A at 75% in exactly the same way, so this is an old race, not a new one. The spec line "This never, on its own, moves you off it" means that setting Manual only does not itself start a switch. In the scenario the switch was started by A's earlier 70% rule, which A had already crossed before he made the change. That matches the spec. The window is also tiny: the founder would have to change the setting inside a single network round trip. The worst outcome is a switch that fits the rule he had seconds earlier, and he can switch back by hand; auto-switch will not bring him back only if A is now Manual only, which is what he asked for. If anyone did count it as a defect, it would be minor.

UPHELD (minor): The code facts check out. Neither window is new, and the founder would almost never hit either one.

Active side: evaluateAutoSwitch reads the active account's rule only before the loop, in plan() and in the log line at AppState.swift:1095-1096. After `await fetchUsageNow(for: target)` (line 1110), the re-check at line 1141 looks only at isLoggingIn, isRefreshing, isSwitching and the active id. So if A is set to Manual only during that fetch, a switch already decided at A's old 70% still goes through. The fetch only runs when the chosen candidate was not sampled this cycle. When it was sampled, there is no await before line 1141 and no window at all.

Target side: the target's threshold is re-read by id after the verification fetch (line 1121, effectiveSwitchThreshold reads `accounts` by id), and ceiling(0) is nil. That covers the fetch window, as spec item 141 says. But switchTo -> performSwitch then awaits provenOwner (an identity call over the network, line 774) and validatedTargetBackup (another identity call, sometimes a token refresh, lines 790 and 908-915). Neither re-checks the threshold before claudeService.switchAccount. So the spec's "cannot be landed on" is slightly overstated for that stretch.

Why it is minor and not a regression:
(1) Both windows already existed for every threshold change before this diff. Raising A from 70 to 95, or B from 50 to 95, during the same awaits behaved the same way. The diff only adds 0 as one more value that can go stale.
(2) To hit it, the founder has to change a threshold in Settings, the CLI or MCP within a window of one to three seconds. That window opens only when a refresh tick first finds a threshold crossed, and at most once per 300-second cooldown. It is a random coincidence, not something normal use reaches.
(3) On the active side, the spec says setting Manual only "never, on its own, moves you off it". That still holds: the move was caused by the 70% threshold he had already crossed, which was the valid rule when the decision was made.
(4) The worst outcome is one switch he would not have wanted. He can undo it by switching back by hand, and the cooldown then stops auto-switch from moving him again. There is no data loss, no crash, and no repeated wrong switching.

A cheap hardening would be one re-read of both rules just before the credential write for automatic switches. That is polish, not a fix the founder needs.

split.title: CLI 'switch' and 'threshold' confirmations say auto-switch will move you off at 90% even when auto-switch is off
split.scenario: With auto-switch turned off, the founder runs `pixelswitch switch 2` on a Manual only account and sees 'Switched to X. It is manual only: auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it.' `pixelswitch accounts threshold <active> manual` likewise adds 'You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at 90%...'. Neither happens, because auto-switch is off. The GUI deliberately hides the same statements when auto-switch is off (SettingsAccountsTab row caption, popover label and card footer are all gated on autoSwitchEnabled), because 'with auto-switch off every account is effectively manual, so a label would mislead'.
split.evidence: CLIRunner.swift:303 `text += " You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at \(percent(account.effectiveThreshold))..."` and CLIRunner.swift:316 `text += " It is manual only: auto-switch moves you off it at ..."`. Neither is conditioned on the auto-switch enabled setting. AccountInfo does not carry it.
split.fix: Fetch status.autoSwitch.enabled (one extra statusGet call, or carry it in the result) and add the 'moves you off it at N%' sentence only when auto-switch is on. When it is off, say 'Auto-switch is off' instead.
verdicts:
REFUTED (minor): The scenario happens as described, but the spec asks for it. CLIRunner.swift:298-320 (CLIOutput.thresholdSet and CLIOutput.switched) adds the "moves you off it at N%" sentence without checking whether auto-switch is on, and the spec says to do exactly that.

- **The spec's remoteControl section defines both messages with no auto-switch condition.** thresholdSet adds "You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it." only "When isActive". switched adds "It is manual only: auto-switch moves you off it at 90%..." "When manualOnly". manualSwitchRule says the same for the CLI confirmation.
- **The spec's tests pin these strings.** The ControlTests entries "cli output: setting manual only says so, and warns when it is the active account" and "cli output: switching to a Manual only account says where it will be left" expect them without any auto-switch condition.
- **The spec gates only the GUI on the auto-switch setting.** The Settings active-row caption and the two popover labels ("WHEN THE LABELS SHOW") need auto-switch on. The CLI section has no such gate. The spec also says the Settings menu label always shows the stored value.
- **This follows how the CLI already behaved before the change.** On main, `accounts threshold` already printed "<email> now switches at 70%." and the `accounts` table already had a "Switches at" column, both regardless of the auto-switch setting (see the removed lines in the diff at CLIRunner.swift:146-154 and :278). In the CLI, the threshold text describes the saved rule for an account, not a promise that auto-switch is running. The new sentences keep that convention.

The code matches the spec word for word, so it is not wrong against the spec. At most it is an optional wording tweak (an "if auto-switch is on" note). If someone wanted that change anyway, it would be minor.

UPHELD (minor): This is real, and minor is the right severity. In PixelSwitchCLI/CLIRunner.swift, CLIOutput.switched (line 316) and CLIOutput.thresholdSet (line 303) decide what to print from AccountInfo alone. AccountInfo (ControlProtocol.swift:382-401) has no auto-switch-enabled field, and neither call site (CLIRunner.swift:94, :149) makes a statusGet call. So with auto-switch off, `pixelswitch switch <manual-only account>` prints "It is manual only: auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it." In the same state, `pixelswitch accounts threshold <active account> manual` adds "You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at 90%...". Neither will happen, because AppState.swift:1054 returns early with `guard autoSwitchEnabled`. The GUI says the same thing only when auto-switch is on: the SettingsAccountsTab caption checks `autoSwitchEnabled && account.isActive && isManualOnly(account)`, and the spec explains why ("with auto-switch off every account is effectively manual, so a label on one account would mislead"). The CLI breaks that rule. Two things keep it minor rather than important. First, the spec (newStrings 18/19, tests 51/52) sets these CLI strings with no condition, so the code matches the spec as written. The gap is in the spec, which applied the auto-switch-off rule to the GUI but not the CLI. Second, the CLI already describes the policy whether or not auto-switch is on: the older "now switches at 70%" message and the "Switches at" column are shown unconditionally too. The only harm is a misleading sentence. No switch happens, and no switching behaviour or data changes.

split.title: Popover 'Manual only' help says 'You can still switch to it here' on the active account, where no switch is possible
split.scenario: Turn auto-switch on and set the account you are using to Manual only. In the popover's Accounts tab, that row has no Switch button (it only appears when !account.isActive). On the Usage tab the double-click does nothing on the active card (canSwitch is false), and for the same reason the hover hint never replaces the label there. Yet both places show 'Manual only' with the help 'Auto-switch never moves you to this account. You can still switch to it here.' On the account you are already on, that help points to an action that does not exist. It also says nothing about the one thing auto-switch still does to this account: moving you off it at the default, which the Settings caption does explain.
split.fix: For the active account, use a different help (or leave it out). For example, reuse the existing key "You're using it now. Auto-switch moves you off it at %@ and won't move you back to it." with the formatted default, and keep the current help for inactive accounts only.
verdicts: REFUTED (minor): The code does what the spec says. The scenario does happen: at AccountSwitcherView.swift:183-189 and UsageDashboardView.swift:376-381 the label has no isActive check, while the Switch button and canSwitch(to:) (UsageDashboardView.swift:330-332) both leave out the active account. So the active Manual only row shows help pointing to a switch you cannot make from that row. But final-spec.json ('otherSurfaces') asks for exactly this. It says: when auto-switch is on and the account is Manual only, show Label("Manual only", systemImage: "hand.raised") with .help("Auto-switch never moves you to this account. You can still switch to it here.") on both the Accounts row and the Usage card footer. It sets no condition on the active account, and its string list names this as the one help text for the popover label. The only condition the spec sets for showing the labels is that auto-switch is on. The spec leaves the explanation for the active account (moved off at the default) to the Settings row caption and the CLI confirmation, and the code does the same. The switching itself is right: nothing moves you onto the account, and on it you are moved off at the default. The finding is a wording request against the spec, not a defect in the code. If the founder wants it changed, it is minor polish: reuse the existing "You're using it now..." key on the active row.

UPHELD (minor): The finding is accurate, but it is only polish. On manual-only, AccountSwitcherView.swift:183-189 and UsageDashboardView.swift:376-381 show the "Manual only" label whenever `autoSwitchEnabled && AutoSwitchSettings.isManualOnly(own: account.switchThreshold)` is true, and neither checks `account.isActive`. The Switch button (`if !account.isActive`) and `canSwitch(to:)` (`!account.isActive && ...`) both leave out the active account. So with auto-switch on and the account you are using set to Manual only, the active row and the active Usage card both show the label. On the card the label is not hidden: the hover-hint branch is skipped because `canSwitch` is false, so the label branch always wins. Hovering either label gives "Auto-switch never moves you to this account. You can still switch to it here." The founder can easily get into this state, since the spec calls out setting Manual only on the account you are using, and the hand-check card asks him to do exactly that. Two things keep it minor. First, the code matches the spec word for word: final-spec.json otherSurfaces gives this help text and the condition "auto-switch is on and the account is Manual only" with no active check, so this is a gap in the spec, not code that departs from it. Second, the visible label "Manual only" is correct. Only the hover tooltip is off, and it is misleading rather than wrong: the account really is never auto-switched to, and you can switch back to it once you leave. The tooltip also leaves out the move-off-at-default rule, but the Settings row caption and the CLI confirmation both explain that. Switching behaviour, data and the build are unaffected.

split.title: Usage tab shows no 'Manual only' marker on a card that has no usage reading (loading or error)
split.scenario: Turn auto-switch on and set an account to Manual only. If that account has no usage yet ('Waiting for usage data...'), or is in an error state such as an expired token or a rate limit, its Usage card shows no 'Manual only' line. The new label lives only in cardFooter, and cardFooter is only built when usage is non-nil. The Accounts tab still shows it, so the two popover tabs disagree for that account until a reading arrives.
split.fix: Draw the same Label in the error and waiting branches as well, trailing in their HStack, under the same autoSwitchEnabled && isManualOnly condition. Or move the Manual only branch into a small helper that all three branches call.
verdicts: REFUTED (minor): The scenario can happen. In UsageDashboardView.swift, lines 238-266, cardFooter(account) is built only in the `if let usage` branch. A card still waiting for data ("Waiting for usage data...") or showing an error (expired, rate limited) has no footer, so it has no "Manual only" line. But the code does what the spec says. Its otherSurfaces section names the place: "POPOVER -> USAGE TAB CARD (UsageDashboardView.cardFooter) A new last branch on the right of the footer shows the same Label and help." Its conditions list only these: not switching, no hover hint, auto-switch on, Manual only. The hand-check card also says "the Usage card footer". The implementation (lines 376-382) is exactly that last branch. The footer's two existing right-side hints, "Switching…" and "Double-click to switch", are already missing on cards in those two states, so the new line behaves the same way as the footer it lives in. The popover Accounts tab (AccountSwitcherView.swift:184) always shows the marker. Switching is not affected: the engine rule is enforced whatever the view shows. At most this is a gap the spec never covered, and it is polish, not a defect against the spec.

UPHELD (minor): This is real, and it is minor. In UsageDashboardView.swift:238-266, cardFooter(account) is only called when `usage` is non-nil, and the new "Manual only" Label (lines 376-381) exists only inside cardFooter. A card with no reading shows only the error HStack or the "Waiting for usage data..." HStack, so the label never appears there.

The founder will actually see this state. AppState.accountUsage is kept only in memory (AppState.swift:15). After every launch, each non-active card waits for the round-robin poll to reach it. AppState also sets accountUsage[id] = nil whenever it records an expired, wrong-account, no-subscription or fetch-failure error (lines 1017, 1194, 1199, 1432, 1463, 1488, 1492, 1503). So a Manual only account with an expired token keeps its label on the Accounts tab (AccountSwitcherView adds it with no usage condition) but has none on its Usage card.

It is not wrong against the spec. The spec says to add the label as "a new last branch on the right of the footer" in cardFooter, and the code does exactly that. The existing "Switching…" and "Double-click to switch" hints are also missing from no-usage cards for the same reason.

The impact is cosmetic. No switching is affected, and nothing is mislabelled; the marker is simply not there. The true value still shows on the Accounts tab and in Settings. Auto-switch also cannot pick a card that has no reading, so leaving the marker off there cannot mislead the founder into expecting a switch that will not happen. It is worth a small follow-up: draw the same Label in the error and waiting branches.

split.title: CLI says auto-switch will move you off a Manual only account even when auto-switch is off
split.scenario: Auto-switch is off (autoSwitch.enabled false). The founder runs `pixelswitch switch 3` on a Manual only account and is told 'It is manual only: auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it.' `pixelswitch accounts threshold <active> manual` adds 'You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at 90%…'. Neither will happen, because auto-switch is off. The GUI hides the matching Settings caption and popover labels when auto-switch is off, for exactly this reason (the spec's rejected list: 'with auto-switch off every account is effectively manual, so a label on one account would mislead'). So the CLI and the GUI disagree.
split.evidence: CLIOutput.thresholdSet (line 302-304) adds the 'You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at …' sentence whenever `account.isActive`. CLIOutput.switched (line 315-316) adds its suffix whenever `account.manualOnly`. Neither looks at autoSwitch.enabled, and CLIRunner.checkProtocol has already decoded a StatusInfo that holds it (status.autoSwitch.enabled).
split.fix: Make checkProtocol return the StatusInfo it decodes (or keep it), and pass `autoSwitchOn` into CLIOutput.thresholdSet and CLIOutput.switched. Add the 'moves you off it at N%' sentences only when it is true; with it off, keep only the first sentence ('… is now manual only: auto-switch never switches to it…'). Add a unit case for each.
verdicts: REFUTED (minor): The scenario does happen: with auto-switch off, CLIOutput.thresholdSet (CLIRunner.swift:300-305) and CLIOutput.switched (313-318) still add the "auto-switch moves you off it at N%" sentence, because neither looks at autoSwitch.enabled. But the spec asks for exactly this. In final-spec.json the remoteControl section defines both strings with no auto-switch condition: thresholdSet adds the sentence "When isActive", and switched adds its suffix "When manualOnly". The spec's test list (ControlTests 'cli output: setting manual only says so, and warns when it is the active account' and 'cli output: switching to a Manual only account says where it will be left') checks those unconditional outputs. The spec gates the auto-switch setting only in two places: the GUI's active-row caption ("When auto-switch is on AND the row is the active account AND it is Manual only") and the popover labels. The rejected-list line the finding quotes is about "Showing the popover 'Manual only' label while auto-switch is off". It does not cover the CLI. The claim that the GUI and CLI disagree is also overstated. The Settings row tooltip (thresholdHelp, applied with .help(thresholdHelp(own:)) and not gated on autoSwitchEnabled) says "while you're on it, auto-switch moves you off it at the default threshold (90%)" whether auto-switch is on or off. Before this change, the CLI accounts table already showed "Switches at 90% (default)" with auto-switch off. So the CLI has always stated auto-switch policy, not whether auto-switch is running. The code matches the spec. At most, gating it would be a small polish change to the spec, not a defect in the code.

UPHELD (minor): The finding is real, but it is minor polish, not a switching defect. The founder would see this text. In human-readable mode (not --json), CLIOutput.thresholdSet (PixelSwitchCLI/CLIRunner.swift:302-304) adds "You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at N% and won't move you back to it." whenever the account is manual only and active. CLIOutput.switched (lines 315-316) adds "It is manual only: auto-switch moves you off it at N%…" whenever the target is manual only. Neither checks autoSwitch.enabled. So with auto-switch off, `pixelswitch switch <manual-only account>` or `pixelswitch accounts threshold <active> manual` prints a sentence about a move that will not happen. The GUI hides the matching Settings caption and popover labels when auto-switch is off (SettingsAccountsTab and AccountSwitcherView/UsageDashboardView gate on autoSwitchEnabled), so the CLI and the GUI do disagree.

Why it is still only minor:
(1) The code does exactly what the spec says. final-spec.json writes both CLI sentences with no auto-switch condition, and the unit tests at Tests/UnitTests/ControlTests.swift:716-724 pin that wording. It is not wrong against the spec; the spec was just less careful here than for the GUI labels.
(2) The CLI always described per-account rules without looking at the on/off state. Before this change, main already printed "<email> now switches at 70%." and the "Switches at" column with auto-switch off, and the new "manual only" legend line does the same. The new sentences follow that habit.
(3) The sentence describes what auto-switch does, and `pixelswitch status` shows "Auto-switch: off". Nothing changes about switching, no data is touched, and --json and MCP output only carry the manualOnly/effectiveThreshold fields, with no prose.

The suggested fix is cheap: keep the StatusInfo that checkProtocol already decodes and pass autoSwitch.enabled into thresholdSet/switched. It is worth doing for consistency, but it is polish, not an important or critical defect.

split.title: A running `pixelswitch mcp` reconnects after the app restarts without re-checking the protocol, so the bump misses stale MCP sessions
split.scenario: Claude on the other Mac has `ssh macA pixelswitch mcp` open, a 1.4 binary that speaks protocol 1. 'Update automatically' is on by default, so the app on Mac A updates to this release and restarts. The next tool call gets .closed; MCPStdio reconnects and retries with no checkProtocol, so there is no mismatch error. The old process goes on serving its old tool list: set_account_threshold still says '(50–100)' with minimum 50 and has no manual only. When the founder asks Claude to make an account manual only, or to set 30%, Claude says it cannot, or keeps within 50. Nothing tells him to restart the session. The version bump was meant to surface exactly this kind of drift.
split.evidence: MCPStdio.run: `if case .closed = error { try client.connect(); connected = true; return try client.call(method, params, timeout: 120) }`. Only the first connect runs `try CLIRunner.checkProtocol(client, timeout: 30)`.
split.fix: After the reconnect in the .closed branch, call `try CLIRunner.checkProtocol(client, timeout: 30)` before setting `connected = true` and retrying. A mismatch then reaches the model as a protocolMismatch tool error instead of silently running with the old schema.
verdicts:
UPHELD (minor): The scenario can happen. In MCPStdio.run (PixelSwitchCLI/MCPServer.swift:239-253), only the first connect calls CLIRunner.checkProtocol. The `.closed` branch reconnects and retries without it. The trigger is real: ControlClient sets SO_NOSIGPIPE, so writing to a socket the old app has closed gives EPIPE, and send() throws ClientError.closed (a read that returns 0 bytes also throws .closed). connect() then runs `open -g -b` to launch the app if needed and attaches to the new one, which speaks protocol 2. From then on the old process (protocol 1) passes results through as raw JSON and never checks the version, so nothing tells the user or the model the session is stale. Its own tool text still says set_account_threshold is 50-100, with minimum 50 and no manual-only option. Claude on the other Mac will therefore keep to 50 or say it cannot make an account manual only.

Three things lower the severity, and none of them refutes the finding:
1. The reconnect code predates this branch. The branch only bumps the version, so this gap would also skip any earlier or later bump.
2. Nothing breaks. The app accepts 0-100 from any client, and list_accounts results pass through with manualOnly included. Only the tool schema and descriptions are stale, and Claude Code caches those from the session's first tools/list in any case.
3. The suggested fix needs care. Calling checkProtocol after the reconnect would make every tool call fail until the MCP session is restarted, because connected stays false and each call re-checks. The error text would say "Quit and reopen PixelSwitch", which does not help: the fix is to restart the `pixelswitch mcp` session. The MCP path should get its own message, something like "this pixelswitch mcp is older than PixelSwitch; restart the MCP session".

The spec's reason for the bump covers the other direction (an old app still running under a new CLI). So this is a real gap, not intended behaviour, but it is minor.

REFUTED (minor): The code path is real, but it causes no wrong result for the founder, it was already there before this change, and the suggested fix would make things worse.

1) It was already there. MCPStdio.run in PixelSwitchCLI/MCPServer.swift (lines 233-265) is not touched by main...manual-only. The reconnect on `.closed` without calling checkProtocol dates from protocol 1. This commit only bumps ControlProtocol.version.

2) An old process talking to the new app gives correct results. Protocol 2 only adds things: AccountInfo gains manualOnly, setThreshold accepts a wider range (0-100 instead of 50-100), and effectiveThreshold is still a Double. MCPServer.run passes the app's reply through untouched: `call(...) -> JSONValue`, then `result.prettyText` and `structuredContent`, with no typed decoding. It also passes arguments through untouched (`pass = { .object($0) }`). So every call a stale 1.4 `pixelswitch mcp` makes still works against the new app. list_accounts even shows the model manualOnly and the new effectiveThreshold. Nothing switches wrongly, no data is lost, and no call fails. The only effect is that the stale session's tool descriptions and schema (minimum 50) do not mention Manual only, so Claude may keep to 50-100.

3) The suggested fix does not help and misleads. The Claude Code MCP client reads tools/list once, when the session starts, and this server never sends list_changed. So even with checkProtocol after the reconnect, the model's tool list stays stale. The fix would only turn every working call into an error. That error's text (CLIRunner.checkProtocol, lines 62-67) says "Quit and reopen PixelSwitch, then run the command again." That is the wrong advice here: the app is already the new version and the stale piece is the MCP process. Following it would change nothing. The founder would get a broken session in place of one that works but does not know about the new feature.

4) Recovery is already automatic. ~/.local/bin/pixelswitch is a symlink into the app bundle (CommandLineToolInstaller.swift:62). So starting a new Claude session on the other Mac starts the updated binary, which checks the protocol on first connect and advertises the 0-100 / Manual only schema.

What is left is at most a pre-existing note: a Claude session that stays open across an app update keeps its old tool descriptions until restarted. That is inherent to how MCP caches tool lists, and it is not a defect in this change.

refuted.title: 'Quit and reopen PixelSwitch' cannot be done with the tool: `pixelswitch quit` and quit_app are refused by the same protocol check
refuted.scenario: This is the first protocol bump, so the first time the mismatch path runs for real. An older app is still running while the bundle (and the ~/.local/bin link into it) has been replaced, for example after a DMG was installed over a running app, or before the post-update restart. Over SSH from the other Mac, every command prints 'PixelSwitch 1.4 speaks remote-control protocol 1, but this pixelswitch speaks 2. Quit and reopen PixelSwitch…'. The obvious step, `pixelswitch quit` (or the MCP quit_app tool), gets the same error, because run() calls checkProtocol before every command except help and version. Remotely the founder has to know to run osascript or pkill.
refuted.evidence: CLIRunner.run: `try client.connect(); try Self.checkProtocol(client, timeout: invocation.timeout); return try execute(invocation)` for every command, including .quit. MCPStdio also checks before any tool, including quit_app. app.quit takes no params and returns {ok:true}, and its shape has not changed across versions.
refuted.fix: Skip checkProtocol for .quit (and for the quit_app tool in MCPStdio), since app.quit is the same in every version. Or extend the mismatch message with a remote-friendly step: 'run `pixelswitch quit`, then any command reopens it'.
verdicts:
REFUTED (minor): The code does what the finding says: in CLIRunner.run (line 45) and MCPStdio, checkProtocol runs before every command, quit and quit_app included. But this branch never touches that code. The diff only changes ControlProtocol.version from 1 to 2. The spec (final-spec.json, remoteControl and risks) looked at this exact outcome and accepted it: "an old app still running after an update then gets the existing 'Quit and reopen PixelSwitch' from CLIRunner.checkProtocol... That is the check working."

The scenario also needs a new bundle sitting under a still-running old app, and the app's own install and update paths prevent that:
(1) Updates go through Sparkle. UpdateChecker.updater(_:willInstallUpdateOnQuit:immediateInstallationBlock:) calls Sparkle's immediate-install block. Sparkle's installer stops the running app first, then swaps the bundle, then relaunches. There is no "before the post-update restart" moment where the new pixelswitch in Contents/Helpers can reach an old process.
(2) The only other install path in the README is dragging the DMG into Applications. As far as I know, Finder will not replace an app that is open (it reports the item is in use). I did not test this.
(3) The CLI reaches the app only through the ~/.local/bin link into that same bundle, so the CLI and the app always come from the same copy.

Getting a mismatch would take a manual cp or ditto over a running app. Even then the founder can get out of it over SSH with `osascript -e 'quit app id "ai.pixelventures.pixelswitch"'` or `pkill -x PixelSwitch`. After that, any pixelswitch command starts the new app again, because ControlClient.connect runs `open -g -b`.

Skipping the check for app.quit would be a reasonable hardening. It is not a defect in this change, and nothing in normal use reaches it.

REFUTED (minor): The code reading is accurate, but the founder will not reach this state in practice, and the gating logic is not new in this branch.

1. The code is as described, but it was already there. CLIRunner.run calls checkProtocol before every command except help and version, and MCPStdio checks on first connect, quit_app included. Both lines already exist on main. The diff changes only `ControlProtocol.version` from 1 to 2, and the protocol's own rule requires that bump because AccountInfo gains `manualOnly`.

2. The mismatch needs an old app still running on top of a new bundle. ~/.local/bin/pixelswitch is a symlink into /Applications/PixelSwitch.app/Contents/Helpers (see CommandLineToolInstaller). So the CLI can only be newer than the app if the bundle is replaced while the old app keeps running. The founder's normal update path cannot produce that:
   - Updates go through Sparkle. "Update automatically" is on by default since 1.4, and the UpdateChecker delegate calls Sparkle's immediateInstallHandler.
   - Sparkle's installer waits for the app to quit, then swaps the bundle, then relaunches. The manual "Install and Relaunch" and install-on-quit paths do the same.
   - During the brief gap before the relaunch, the CLI finds no socket and runs `open -b ...`, which starts the new v2 app. That is a protocol match.
   - The "post-update restart" scenario in the finding does not exist, because the bundle is replaced only after the old process is gone.

3. The DMG scenario is essentially unreachable. The README's install path is dragging from the DMG into Applications. Finder normally refuses to replace an app that is open, with a "can't be replaced because it's open" error. So a v1 app on top of a v2 bundle needs a manual `cp`/`ditto` over a running app, or a developer build running from DerivedData. That is developer territory, not something the founder does as a user.

4. If it did happen, the harm is small. Locally he can quit from the menu bar. Remotely, `osascript -e 'quit app "PixelSwitch"'` or `pkill PixelSwitch` works, and then any pixelswitch command relaunches the app, because ControlClient.connect runs `open -g -b`. No switching goes wrong and no data is lost.

5. The suggested fix would not cover the one related case that is somewhat plausible. That case is a long-running MCP server process started over SSH before the update: it keeps running the old v1 code in memory. Even there, MCPStdio's reconnect after a `.closed` error skips checkProtocol entirely, so tool calls usually carry on against the v2 app. Where the mismatch does show, it comes from the already-shipped v1 binary, which this diff cannot change. Skipping the check for quit_app in v2 code would not help that case.

If the scenario is forced anyway (a manual copy over a running app), the result is a minor polish issue: an error message that is awkward to follow remotely. It is not wrong behaviour.

refuted.title: A fraction sent for a percentage now silently becomes Manual only or 'Switch at 1%' instead of being refused
refuted.scenario: Over MCP the founder says 'set account 2 to 80%', and the model sends {"threshold": 0.8}, a fraction mix-up models often make. Before this change, 50–100 refused 0.8 and the model corrected itself. Now 0.8 rounds to 1, so account 2 becomes 'Switch at 1%': if it is active, auto-switch moves him off it at 1% right after the cooldown, and as a target it qualifies only at 0.5% or less. A value of 0.3 rounds to 0 and silently makes the account Manual only. The response carries threshold 1 or 0, but nothing flags it as a likely mistake.
refuted.evidence: `guard value.isFinite, AutoSwitchSettings.accountThresholdRange.contains(value.rounded()) else { throw … }; threshold = value.rounded()`. With accountThresholdRange 0...100, every value from 0 to 1.49 is accepted. The MCP schema is `minimum 0, maximum 100` with no whole-number hint.
refuted.fix: Keep rounding for normal values, but refuse 0 < value < 1 with invalidValue: 'Thresholds are percentages: 1–100 (80 means 80%), or 0 for manual only.' Optionally add `"multipleOf": 1` or 'a whole percentage, e.g. 80 for 80%' to the set_account_threshold schema and description. This goes against the spec's '0.4 → manual only, 0.6 → 1' line, so update that test and record it as a decision.
verdicts:
REFUTED (minor): The code does what the spec asks. The spec's remoteControl section (final-spec.json line 44) names this exact guard and message and says "0.4 becomes 0 (manual only); 0.6 becomes 1; 35 is accepted; -1 and 101 are refused". Line 142 records the same rounding as intended, and line 92 lists a test for it. ControlAPI.swift:155 matches the spec word for word, and ControlTests.swift:359-363 ("api: 0.4 rounds to manual only and 0.6 to 1") pins it. The finding says itself that its fix "goes against the spec's '0.4 → manual only, 0.6 → 1' line". So it asks for a design change, not a fix for a defect.

The scenario also depends on a model that ignores the tool's own contract. The set_account_threshold description (MCPServer.swift:82) opens with "Set the usage percentage (1–100)" and describes 0 as manual only, so a model is told the unit is whole percentage points. Every set call also returns the updated AccountInfo, with threshold, effectiveThreshold and manualOnly, so a wrong value shows up in the reply right away.

Refusing 0 < value < 1 would be a hardening choice to guard against a guessed model mistake. If the founder wants it, it belongs in a decision record, not in a bug report against this change.

REFUTED (minor): The code does exactly what the spec asks. It is not a defect against the spec: final-spec.json remoteControl says "0.4 becomes 0 (manual only); 0.6 becomes 1; 35 is accepted; -1 and 101 are refused". The spec's test list includes "api: 0.4 rounds to manual only and 0.6 to 1", and that test is in Tests/UnitTests/ControlTests.swift:359-363. The finding's own fix admits this goes against the spec. What it really proposes is a design change.

Reaching it from the founder's side takes a model error that the surrounding contract works against:
- The set_account_threshold description opens with "Set the usage percentage (1–100)". It also says "at least 10 points under its own threshold" and "100 uses the account until it is empty".
- Every percentage the protocol returns uses 0–100: UsageInfo.utilization is documented "Percent used, 0–100", and effectiveThreshold is 0–100. So a model reading get_usage or list_accounts sees 80, not 0.8, before it writes anything.
- The CLI is not affected in practice: the founder would type "80", not "0.8".

If it did happen, it would not be silent. The setThreshold response returns the account with threshold 1 (or 0 and manualOnly true), and any sensible model reports "now switches at 1%". Settings then shows "Switch at 1%" or "Manual only" on that row, and `pixelswitch accounts` shows it in the Switches at column.

The worst outcome is an ordinary auto-switch to another eligible account, or an account that is never switched to automatically. Both are reversible with one menu pick, and nothing is lost. The old 50–100 guard refused 0.8 only because 50 happened to be the floor, not by design. At most this is optional hardening: refuse 0 < value < 1, or add "a whole percentage, e.g. 80" to the schema. It is not a bug the founder would hit.

refuted.title: Choosing Manual only on the account you are using can move you off it within minutes, which the spec says never happens
refuted.scenario: The active account is on 'Switch at 100%' (use it until empty), usage is at 93%, and the default is 90%. The founder picks 'Manual only (0%)' for that account. plan() now leaves the account at leaveAtThreshold(0, 90) = 90, so at the next refresh (with no switch in the last 5 minutes) 93 >= 90 fires and auto-switch moves him off. Before the change he would have stayed until 100%. The Settings row caption and the CLI confirmation both say 'Auto-switch moves you off it at 90%' even though he is already past that. The spec's manualSwitchRule says 'This never, on its own, moves you off it', and its rejected list says a settings change should not pull a live login out from under running sessions.
refuted.evidence: let activeThreshold = AutoSwitchSettings.leaveAtThreshold(rule: activeRule, defaultThreshold: defaultThreshold) (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:277) together with the trigger `activeUtil >= activeThreshold`. Choosing Manual only drops the leave point from the account's old custom value to the global default. Neither SettingsAccountsTab (caption at line ~93) nor CLIOutput.thresholdSet checks current usage against that value.
refuted.fix: The spec contradicts itself here, so the founder should choose. One option is to leave an active Manual only account at max(default, its previous custom value); that value is not stored, so it would mean keeping the previous threshold until the account is no longer active. Another is to keep the engine as it is and have the caption and CLI say you will be moved at the next check when usage is already at or above the default. At minimum, record the case in the decision notes the spec asks for, so it is known and deliberate.
verdicts:
REFUTED (minor): The scenario can happen, but the code does what the spec intends, so I am refuting it as a defect.

What the code does:
- setSwitchThreshold (AppState.swift:666-680) only saves the new value. It starts no auto-switch check, so picking Manual only never moves you off on the spot. That is the thing spec rejected[14] rules out.
- At the next refresh, plan() uses leaveAtThreshold(rule: 0, default: 90), which returns 90 (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:501-503). If usage is already 93%, auto-switch moves you off.

Why that matches the spec:
- spec.oneLine says: "while you are on it auto-switch moves you off only at the default threshold".
- spec.manualSwitchRule "NO HIDDEN STATE" says the same rule applies however the account became active, and lists "you set Manual only on the account you are on" first.
- spec.zeroSemantics and grafted[1] say plan() reads 0 on the active account as "leave at defaultThreshold".
- Spec test 4 pins leaveAtThreshold(0, 90) == 90.
- Remembering the old 100% leave point would need stored state ("picked by you" / the previous threshold). The spec rejected that on purpose (rejected[1]), so leaving at the default is a known, chosen consequence.

About the "never, on its own, moves you off it" sentence: the spec pairs it with the caption "Auto-switch moves you off it at 90%". So it means the setting is not itself a reason to leave, not that the old leave point is kept. In the scenario you are moved because usage has already reached the leave point the spec names. The Settings caption and the CLI line (CLIOutput.thresholdSet) state that 90% correctly. The same thing happens when a custom threshold is lowered below current usage; Manual only is not special here.

What is left is polish only: the caption could say "at the next check" when usage is already past the default. That is not wrong behaviour and not a false message.

refuted.title: The plan-level tests that say Manual only is never an early-drain target would still pass if the exclusion were removed
refuted.scenario: Say someone later removes the nil guard from ceiling(), so ceiling(0, 1) returns 0 - min(1, 0) = 0, or restores the old 'threshold - drainMinimumRoom', which gives -1. The tests 'rules: manual only: never an early-drain target' and the drain half of 'rules: ping-pong: nothing brings you back to a Manual only account' still pass. They put m0 at sample(10, 80, weeklyResetsIn: 12) and sample(10, 10, weeklyResetsIn: 12), and a busy account is never under a 0 or -1 ceiling. The tests' names say they prove the drain exclusion, but they cannot fail when it breaks. Only the direct eligibleUtilization check in 'verification refuses it under both rules' (sample(0,0)) actually tests it.
refuted.evidence: let drainUsage = [aDefault.id: sample(30, 40), m0.id: sample(10, 80, weeklyResetsIn: 12), ...] (line 125) and the ping-pong case m0.id: sample(10, 10, weeklyResetsIn: 12) (line 163). The spec prescribed these numbers, which carry the same weakness.
refuted.fix: Give m0 an untouched reading in both plan-level drain cases, sample(0, 0, weeklyResetsIn: 12), and keep the default-account control (y) at the same reading. The plan will then pick M if Manual only ever becomes eligible for a drain.
verdicts:
REFUTED (none): The arithmetic in the finding is right, but it does not describe a defect under this review's rules. Nobody using the app would ever hit it, and the code follows the spec.

1. **The tests match the spec.** final-spec.json says 'never an early-drain target' should put m0 at sample(10,80, weeklyResetsIn: 12) and the same reading on a default account y. The test uses exactly those numbers. For the ping-pong drain half, the spec only asks for "m0 resetting in 12 h", and sample(10,10, weeklyResetsIn: 12) satisfies that.

2. **The shipped code excludes Manual only correctly.** AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling returns nil when threshold <= manualOnlyThreshold. Both drainEligibleUtilization and the .threshold branch of eligibleUtilization bail out on that nil before reading any usage. So a Manual only candidate is never a drain or threshold target, whatever its usage.

3. **The regression the finding imagines is already caught elsewhere.** If someone removed the nil guard, ceiling(0, 1) would return 0. Three existing tests would then fail:
   - ceilingTests checks `ceiling(0, 10) == nil && ceiling(0, 1) == nil ...` directly.
   - 'manual only: verification refuses it under both rules' calls the drain path with sample(0,0, weeklyResetsIn: 12), threshold 0 and the active reset 100 h out. Without the guard, 0 <= 0 would make that reading eligible and the test would fail.
   - Every threshold-trigger plan test puts m0 at sample(0,0). Without the guard, ceiling(0, 10) is also 0, so those tests fail too.

4. **The other variant is harmless.** Restoring 'threshold - drainMinimumRoom' gives a ceiling of -1. That still excludes every reading, including 0%, so behaviour stays correct and there is nothing to catch.

5. **The plan-level drain test does guard one real regression.** If 0 were ever treated as "use the default", the ceiling would be 89, m0 at 80 would become eligible, and the test would fail.

What remains is a test that is not as strong as its name suggests. That is a test-quality preference, not wrong behaviour, a misleading message, or a gap against the spec.

REFUTED (none): The founder would never see this in the app, the CLI or MCP, and the code is not wrong against the spec. What the reviewer says about the tests is true, but it does not describe a defect.

1. The running code is correct. rankedTargets excludes an account only when eligibleUtilization returns nil. For an early drain, that goes through drainEligibleUtilization, which starts with `guard let ceiling = Self.ceiling(threshold: threshold, room: drainMinimumRoom)`. For 0 or NaN, ceiling() returns nil (`guard threshold > AutoSwitchSettings.manualOnlyThreshold`). So a Manual only account can never be a drain target today, whatever its readings.

2. The tests match the spec word for word. final-spec.json prescribes these cases: "m0 at sample(10,80, weeklyResetsIn: 12) gives 'stay'. The same sample on a default y gives 'windows/drainEarly: Y'", and the ping-pong case. The finding admits the spec prescribed these numbers.

3. The regression the reviewer worries about is already caught elsewhere. The only change that would make Manual only drain-eligible is dropping the nil guard, which gives ceiling(0,1) = 0, so an account at exactly 0% on both windows would pass. Two tests would fail:
   - ceilingTests asserts `ceiling(0, 10) == nil && ceiling(0, 1) == nil && ceiling(-5, 10) == nil && ceiling(.nan, 10) == nil`.
   - 'manual only: verification refuses it under both rules' calls eligibleUtilization(sample(0, 0, weeklyResetsIn: 12), trigger: .drainEarly, threshold: 0) and expects nil.
   The reviewer's other example, going back to 'threshold - drainMinimumRoom', gives a ceiling of -1. That still leaves every Manual only account ineligible, because usage is never below 0, so it would not change behaviour at all.

What is left is a note that the plan-level test names claim more than their inputs prove. Using sample(0,0) there would add some redundancy, but that is optional test hardening, not a wrong result, a crash or a gap in the spec.

refuted.title: Spec items not in the branch: the 1.5 hand-check card, the 1.5 release-note warning and the decision records
refuted.scenario: The spec's tests list includes a 'Hand-check card on the 1.5 release page': menu order, the Stepper stopping at 1, tooltips, captions, the popover lines, confirming the active account is NOT moved off, and the CLI steps. storageAndMigration says the 1.5 release notes must warn that Manual only and thresholds below 50% need 1.5 or later, because a hand-installed 1.4 reads 0 and 1-49 as 50. The spec also says, twice, to record as decisions that nothing is remembered when Manual only is chosen, that there is no confirmation, and that setting Manual only on the active account does not move you. The branch changes only code, README and strings. docs/decisions/pixelswitch-hand-checks-2026-09-25.html, RELEASE_NOTES.md (still 1.4) and any decision record are untouched. Only the 'no off/never/disable alias' decision is written down, in a comment in CLIParser. If /release runs from this branch as it is, CI publishes RELEASE_NOTES.md as the release body, so the downgrade warning and the hand-check card would be missing.
refuted.evidence: git diff main...manual-only --stat lists no file under docs/ and no RELEASE_NOTES.md. RELEASE_NOTES.md begins '## PixelSwitch 1.4'. .github/workflows/build.yml:216-220 uses the committed RELEASE_NOTES.md as the single source.
refuted.fix: Before release, add the Manual only card to the hand-check page, write the 1.5 notes with the 'needs 1.5 or later' warning, and record the no-memory, no-confirmation and does-not-move-you-off decisions with their reasons (the decisions surface or the worklog), so a later session does not 'fix' them.
verdicts:
REFUTED (minor): This is not a defect in the branch. The finding treats release-time work and decision records as if the feature commit had to contain them, and each part is either handled by the release process or already done.

1. RELEASE_NOTES.md: step 3 of .claude/commands/release.md is marked "REQUIRED — do this BEFORE tagging". It overwrites RELEASE_NOTES.md and commits it as its own commit ("docs: Release notes for X.Y") before scripts/release.sh creates the tag. Every past release in the history follows this: de4a299 for 1.2, 08f1b63 for 1.3, fe76a98 for 1.4. Each is a separate commit after the feature commit. The feature commits (b68b074, 6d3651f) never touched RELEASE_NOTES.md. So "CI publishes the stale 1.4 notes" can only happen if someone skips a required step of /release. The branch does not cause it. The spec itself says "the 1.5 release notes should say...", which is release-time work.

2. The hand-check card: the history shows the hand-check page is updated at release time, not in the feature commit. For 1.3 it came after the bump (b582a59 "Hand-check page for 1.3"). For 1.4 it went into the release-notes commit (fe76a98 "hand-check page follows"). The spec lists it as a "Hand-check card on the 1.5 release page", tied to the release, and no 1.5 release exists yet.

3. The decision records are already written. The working tree has an uncommitted change to docs/decisions/2026-09-24-remote-control-answers.md. It adds a section "Per-account thresholds down to 0% (Manual only), 2026-09-26" with the founder's request verbatim and a list headed "Decisions NOT to do something". That list records the no-remembered-threshold decision and the "setting Manual only on the account you are using does not move you off it" decision, each with its reason. It also covers the checkbox, the cooldown, the CLI aliases, the badge and the global default. The spec says "Record it as a decision" only for those two items, not for "no confirmation". "There is no confirmation" appears only as a behaviour statement in manualSwitchRule and otherSurfaces. The claim that the spec says "twice" to record three decisions is wrong.

Nothing the user sees in the app, CLI or MCP is wrong because of this. At most there is a housekeeping point: the decision-record edit is not committed yet, and the 1.5 notes and hand-check card still have to be written during /release, which the process already requires.

REFUTED (minor): The founder would not see any of this in the app, the CLI or MCP, and the release scenario the finding describes cannot happen.

1. Releasing from this branch is impossible. scripts/release.sh stops with "Must be on main branch" unless the current branch is main. Step 3 of .claude/commands/release.md (/release) requires RELEASE_NOTES.md to be overwritten and committed before tagging. So a 1.5 tag can never ship the stale 1.4 body.

2. Release notes and the hand-check page are written at release time on main, never on a feature branch. That is the repo's established pattern:
   - fe76a98 "docs: Release notes for 1.4; hand-check page follows" changes only RELEASE_NOTES.md and docs/decisions/pixelswitch-hand-checks-2026-09-25.html.
   - 08f1b63 and b582a59 did the same for 1.3.
   - de4a299 and b613e67 did the same for 1.2.
   Their absence from a feature commit is expected.

3. The decision records do exist. They are uncommitted in the working tree: `M docs/decisions/2026-09-24-remote-control-answers.md` gains a section titled "Per-account thresholds down to 0% ("Manual only"), 2026-09-26". It holds the founder's words verbatim and lists the decisions not to do something:
   - no checkbox;
   - setting Manual only on the active account does not move you off it;
   - no remembered previous threshold;
   - no off/never/disable aliases;
   - no badge beside the name;
   - the global default cannot go below 50.
   The spec never asks for "no confirmation" to be recorded as a decision. It only states it as behaviour.

What is left is housekeeping, not a user-facing defect:
- That decision section is not yet committed.
- Neither the decision section nor the worklog mentions the "Manual only and thresholds below 50% need 1.5 or later" warning. The release-notes writer has to carry it over from the spec. Even if it were missed, the founder would only notice after hand-installing an older 1.4 DMG, which is unlikely now that Update automatically is on by default.

Both points are minor process items for release time.
